item.title: Trump announces new 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks and steel
item.description:
President Donald Trump threatened to raise automobile tariffs on Canada to 50% as the trade rift and political slanging match between the neighboring nations escalated. Trump announced Monday morning that U.S. tariffs on all Canadian cars and trucks, automotive parts, and steel will increase to 50% starting Jan. 1, 2027. “Build in the U.S. and there are zero tariffs. Trump’s comments came after trade talks between the two countries broke down , with each side accusing the other of making eleventh-hour demands that derailed negotiations. “They feel entitled, and yet, we don’t need Canada, they need us!” the President said, repeating his accusation that “Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years.”…

item.description:

item.title: Study: Most Mealtime Screen Time Is TV, Not Social Media
item.description:
Everyone has seen them out at restaurants: the "iPad babies" and zoned-out families. Parents letting their children, some quite young, stare at phones or tablets throughout the meal, sometimes while mom and dad also look at screens. It's easy to judge those families, though I try to remind myself that we, as casual onlookers, never know the full story. Maybe this almost never happens but tonight the parent has a crucial work deadline. Maybe it's been that rare kind of extraordinarily stressful day. Maybe that boy has developmental issues and this is the only way he can get through a restaurant meal, which the family needs to do because they're traveling. Maybe, whatever the reason, this is an anomaly and not the mealtime norm. But screen time during meals may be the norm for many families, according to some new research published in JAMA Pediatrics . The Department of Homeland Security's proposed rule would charge $103,265 as an additional fee for every H-1B petition subject to the annual statutory cap, including petitions eligible for the advanced-degree exemption. The worker visas are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research industries. The fee would be used to cover the federal government’s costs of administering the legal immigration system , including actions carried out by DHS and the Department of Justice, Department of State and Department of Labor. item.title: Tyler Cowen: The Least Bad Way to Regulate AI
item.description:
For how much longer will the fate of American artificial intelligence be steered from Silicon Valley rather than Washington? To watch the pace of AI progress, one might imagine that the answer to that question is rapidly shortening. Each milestone in the capability of AI increases the desire among lawmakers and much of the public to rein in the technology. That includes positive breakthroughs, such as the declaration last week by payments company Stripe that AI has achieved the long-awaited “singularity”: the ability to improve itself beyond what humans can contribute. It also includes worrying episodes, like the breach of the AI database Hugging Face last month by a powerful model gone rogue. Yet for all of the risks that AI brings, the harm caused by overregulating it would likely be much worse for the public. That is why AI developers and experts are devising proposals to promote AI…
